scope.summary: This standard specifies the physical, mechanical, surface-coating, and fire-retardant requirements, along with corresponding test methods, for flat Aluminium Composite Panels (ACP) utilized in building construction. It covers panels intended for external applications (such as cladding façades, curtain walls, soffits, canopies, and high mast monoliths), internal use (such as partitions, ceilings, and column encasements), transportation applications (such as railway coach furnishings), and fire-retardant panels with various properties matching their specific application environments.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Building Panels / Light Metals & Alloys)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Aluminium Composite Panels manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, stocking, or selling non-certified cladding panels in the domestic market is a punishable offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Micro and small units are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic building cladding panels.

requirements.detail: Every panel must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) marked legibly and indelibly on its reverse face or secure label, accompanied by the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 17682).

The composite panel must consist of three main structural layers: a top and a bottom coated aluminium sheet, and an in-between core layer made either of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) or mineral-based fire-retardant material, bonded together using high-performance adhesive films.
Panels are classified into six distinct application grades to match structural and fire demands: Grade 1, Grade 2, Grade 2S, Grade 3, Grade 4, and Grade 5.

The standard specifies three nominal size configurations: a) 1 200 mm × 2 400 mm; b) 1 200 mm × 3 050 mm; c) 1 200 mm × 3 660 mm. The nominal sheet thicknesses are 2 mm, 3 mm, 4 mm, 5 mm, and 6 mm. Other dimensions can be mutually agreed between manufacturer and buyer.

Finished panel dimensions must satisfy: Length tolerance of +4 mm, width tolerance of +2 mm. Thickness tolerances: less than 3 mm is ±0.1 mm; 3 mm and above is ±0.2 mm. Edge straightness deviation must not exceed ±0.5 percent (tested per Annex C), and squareness deviation is limited to a maximum of ±5 mm (tested per Annex C).
Manufacturers must verify raw materials: polymer granules (Clause 5.1), aluminium alloy sheets (Clause 5.2), and surface coating parameters (Clause 5.4).

Finished panels must satisfy physical-mechanical limits: core polymer density, aluminium sheet tensile strength, yield strength, elongation, and joint T-peel strength (testing adhesive bond integrity between the core and aluminium sheets).

Coatings must undergo strict quality audits: dry coating thickness, cross-cut adhesion, pencil hardness, specular gloss, color/gloss retention, and accelerated weathering under the updated weathering test IS 101 (Part 6/Sec 5) [1].

For fire-retardant panels (Grade FR), the composite assembly must undergo fire testing to verify: Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) to check combustion limits, Smoke Density Rating to measure toxic fumes, Ignitability, and Surface Flame Spread behavior.
When requested by the specifier, panels must pass optional engineering tests to certify Sound Transmission Class (STC) ratings, sound absorption coefficients, and thermal conductivity coefficients.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17682 : 2021 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification establishing the quality, dimensions, coating durability, and fire safety requirements for flat Aluminium Composite Panels (ACP or cladding sheets) used in building exteriors (facades, curtain walls, canopies) and interior partitions. Under the national 'Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products Quality Control Order', all ACP panels supplied in India must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). The panels consist of top and bottom coated aluminium skins bonded to a low-density polyethylene (LDPE) or fire-retardant mineral-based core. It regulates dimensional tolerances, coating types (such as weather-resistant PVDF or FEVE), mechanical bonding (peel strength), and critical fire retardancy parameters (such as limiting oxygen index and low smoke density) to protect high-rise structures from fire spread. Amendment No. 2 (December 2025) updates the weathering and durability protocols by aligning them with advanced paint testing standards [1].
